newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Kengo says battles lost, not war.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Kengo says battles lost, not war.

text.p: Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo said on Wednesday that the army may have lost battles to Tutsi-led rebels in the east but it had not lost the war.
With the two sides facing up for a showdown over Zaire's strategic third city of Kisangani, Kengo rejected suggestions that the city was about the fall.
Asked to account for a catalogue of army defeats since the rebels took up arms in October, he took a veiled swipe at Zaire's army commanders.

"You know since Caesar's time it is said that there are no bad troops. I'll let you finish the phrase," he told a news conference. The famous military saying states there are no bad troops, only bad commanders.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila, a veteran opponent of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, has given the army until Thursday to lay down its arms.
"Kabila has won battles but he has not won the war," Kengo said. "The advantage of Zaire is it's size."
He accused the international press of prematurely predicting the fall of Kisangani, headquarters of army operations in the war zone. "The rebels are not at the gates of Kisangani," he said.
The rebels took up arms accusing Zairean authorities of denying them citizenship and seeking to expel them. They hold towns and territory in the east and have pushed west and south.
Mobutu, who had prostate cancer surgery in Europe in August, is in France. He has spent most of his time there since August.
